inspection_summary: Inspected all 143 normalized lines. The paper proposes a closure/induction principle for Bombieri-type equidistribution under multiplicative convolution, sketches a proof by decomposing the convolution error and treating a smoothed character expression differently at small and large conductor, notes avoidance of an imprimitive-character obstruction in Chen's arrangement, and derives iterated applications to divisor functions, restricted prime products, and additive divisor asymptotics. Several hypotheses and displayed formulas are damaged by extraction, so accepted claims are limited to what the surrounding prose makes recoverable and formula-dependent details are flagged for scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Bombieri-type equidistribution is closed under multiplicative convolution
accepted_units.why_material: This is the paper's reusable induction step: once two arithmetic functions satisfy the stated growth, character-sum, and progression-distribution conditions, their multiplicative convolution remains in the same class, allowing new equidistributed sequences to be built compositionally.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 15-20 supply the generalization/induction motivation; lines 21-43 introduce the three hypotheses; lines 44-45 state the closure theorem. The symbols in two hypotheses and parts of the error term are extraction-damaged, so the exact quantitative contract needs the page image before downstream formal reuse.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The semantic closure claim is prose-recoverable, but the exact bounds, conductor condition, and notation for the three properties depend on damaged displayed mathematics and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Decompose convolution error at complementary logarithmic cutoffs
accepted_units.why_material: The proof starts from an explicit identity that reorganizes the progression error of the convolution into pieces involving one factor times the other's error term, with complementary cutoff ranges; the text then says the outer sums are directly estimated by the preserved equidistribution property. This is the mechanism that makes the closure theorem inductive rather than a black-box assertion.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed identity across lines 48-66 is only partly legible, while line 66 preserves the inverse-residue relation and lines 72-73 identify immediate property-(C) estimates. The unit crosses the page marker solely to retain the sentence that disposes of the first pieces.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence: the cutoff exponents, summation limits, and individual terms must be checked against the scan; only the structural decomposition and its stated control by property (C) are safe from the normalized prose.

accepted_units.title: Smooth the residual term and split characters by conductor
accepted_units.why_material: The remaining contribution is handled through a second Riesz mean expressed using characters and a line integral, after which smoothing and character estimates are routed by conductor size: the relevant hypothesis treats small conductor, while a large-sieve argument combined with Chen's integrand division treats large conductor. This is a reusable division-of-labor pattern between local character information and averaged spectral control.
accepted_units.context_note: The integral at lines 77-81 and the labels of the properties at lines 82-84 are extraction-damaged, but the conductor split and the large-sieve/Chen strategy are explicit in prose at lines 82-86. The proof is announced as a sketch, with details deferred at lines 90-93.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate-to-high formula dependence. The qualitative strategy is recoverable; the precise Riesz kernel, Dirichlet series, contour parameter, and which named hypothesis enters each step require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The rearranged proof avoids Chen's imprimitive-character obstruction
accepted_units.why_material: The author contrasts the proposed procedure with Chen's integrand-dividing argument and stresses that a known obstruction from imprimitive characters does not arise, yielding at the same time a simplified route to Chen's binary Goldbach theorem. This identifies not just a technique but the obstacle the technique is designed to remove.
accepted_units.context_note: The claim is explicit prose, nested inside the conductor-split proof sketch. The source supplies no detailed verification here and sends the full proof elsewhere.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low for the stated comparative claim, but validating why the obstruction disappears depends on omitted proof details rather than on this normalized text alone.

accepted_units.title: Closure bootstraps the constant function to higher divisor functions
accepted_units.why_material: The constant function is asserted to satisfy all three hypotheses, so repeated convolution transfers the Bombieri analogue to the k-th divisor function. The same closure perspective is then described as extending earlier theorems and enabling iteration of Bombieri's theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the clearest direct demonstration of the theorem as an induction principle rather than a one-off estimate. Some cited theorem labels are degraded, but the constant-function-to-divisor-function route is legible.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low for the inductive mechanism; exact correspondence with the cited German/Fujii theorem labels would require cleaner bibliographic typography.

accepted_units.title: Equidistribution for indicator sequences of restricted prime products
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 packages iteration into a new family: an indicator for integers representable as a product of a fixed number of primes constrained to specified size ranges inherits property (C), uniformly over the range parameters. The text identifies earlier estimates used in Chen's argument and improvements of Fujii's results as special cases.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 100-101 explain why the result is stated separately; lines 102-108 give the theorem; lines 109-110 place known cases inside it. Several parameter symbols and inequalities in lines 102-108 are corrupted, so only the family-level statement is reliable without the scan.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the exact admissibility inequalities and uniformity domain; low-to-moderate for the semantic statement that iterated convolution controls structured products of primes.

accepted_units.title: Iterated equidistribution feeds additive-divisor asymptotics with uneven coefficient difficulty
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 is said to yield asymptotic expansions in additive divisor problems for prime-product inputs. The author separately observes that some displayed coefficients are easy to calculate whereas the remaining coefficients require substantial work, distinguishing availability of an expansion from tractability of all its constants.
accepted_units.context_note: The existence and qualitative structure of the application are explicit at lines 111-112 and 120-129, but both displayed expansions at lines 113-119 and coefficient names at lines 121-122 are badly extracted. The page header at lines 123-126 interrupts the sentence without changing its meaning.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high for the actual asymptotic formulas, error terms, and coefficient identities; those details must not be used without scan verification. Only the prose-level implication and coefficient-complexity contrast are accepted here.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A compositional route from equidistribution axioms to structured sequences
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Closure under multiplicative convolution turns one verified base sequence into a hierarchy of divisor-function and restricted-prime-product sequences, so the theorem functions as a semantic constructor for new equidistribution results.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The normalized source does not preserve the exact quantitative hypotheses or the prime-range inequalities well enough to instantiate the constructor numerically without scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Why the closure proof needs two analytic regimes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The convolution identity isolates pieces directly controlled by progression equidistribution and a residual smoothed character term; splitting the latter by conductor routes small and large characters to different hypotheses and tools.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a strategy-level synthesis from the proof sketch; the displayed identity and integral are degraded and the detailed estimates are deferred outside the source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Obstacle-aware reuse of Chen's device
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Motohashi retains Chen's integrand-division device in the large-conductor regime while reorganizing the surrounding procedure so that the imprimitive-character obstruction is claimed not to appear, broadening the same analytic engine to iterated prime-product estimates.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source asserts but does not prove locally that the obstruction disappears, so this relation is a candidate mechanism rather than independently verified evidence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Downstream reach exceeds coefficient accessibility
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Equidistribution for structured prime products can be transferred into additive-divisor asymptotics even when extracting all coefficients remains substantially harder than establishing the expansion's broad form.
